name: Database per Service Pattern
forces_resolved: Complete data isolation and loose coupling: services cannot access each other's databases directly
Independent schema migrations and database upgrades with zero cross-team blockers
Polyglot persistence: each service chooses the optimal data store (RDBMS, Document, Graph, Time-Series)
forces_unresolved: Loss of cross-domain ACID transactions and foreign key constraints
Complex distributed queries requiring API composition or CQRS view stores
Higher operational overhead of managing multiple database clusters or schemas
applicability_conditions: True microservices deployments where independent service deployability is non-negotiable
Domains with differing storage paradigms (e.g., Relational for billing, MongoDB for product catalog)
Strict multi-tenant security boundaries requiring separate physical databases per service
anti_requisites: Strict requirement for immediate atomic relational joins across core business tables
Small engineering team without dedicated DBA / infrastructure support
Budget constraints unable to sustain multiple hosted database instances
